title: Pasadena City Council, 2006-09-11, item 6C Part 1: appeal of building official's denial of wood-shake roofing (3 South Grand Avenue)
code_edition: California Building Code 2001 with Pasadena modifications (stated in staff report p.3)
document_date: 2006-09-11 hearing (printed on p.1); attachment memo dated 2006-07-24 (rendered p.9)

facts.text: Agenda subject line (text layer clipped at line ends): appeal of the building official's denial of alternative roofing materials at the Vista del Arroyo Bungalows, 3 South Grand Avenue; hearing date printed as 2006-09-11; Council may uphold the denial or overturn it.

Executive summary: wood-shake roofing was installed on four structures in violation of City ordinance and of the approved building plans and permits (the text layer is clipped at line ends; 'approved' is inferred from context); the developer requested after-the-fact approval as an alternate material under the State Historical Building Code.

Approved plans showed a new cementitious shingle-type roof; the City adopted the 2001 CBC with modifications, and PMC 14.04.020 #6 prohibits wood shake or wood roof covering in high fire hazard zones.

Developer's proposed mitigation (fire-retardant shingles, sprinklers, hydrants, electrical updates, spark arresters, HOA landscape maintenance) and the staff finding that none of these factors is proven sufficient for wood roofing in this zone.
Fire Chief letter (Attachment E) states the Fire Chief lacks authority to grant an exemption to the Municipal Code.

SHBSB letter of 2006-04-27 (Attachment F) indicated wood shake is allowed on state-historic structures; SHBSB determined the Glendale case should be reconsidered (Attachments G and H); the report says that case remains pending.

Attachment index lists A (City Attorney memo), B (PMC 14.04.020 #6), C (historical fire facts), D (letter to Fire Chief), E (denial), F (SHBSB approval), G (Glendale documentation), H (reconsideration request), I (site photos).
City Attorney memo continuation (rendered; dated 2006-07-24): 'The Building Official Does Not Have Authority To Allow That Which Is Prohibited.'
Attachment C (rendered): a web printout, 'Shingles and Shakes', dated 2006-06-22.

Attachment H (rendered): Building Official letter of 2006-06-15 to the SHBSB executive director, stating the City will continue to enforce its building code prohibition on wood roofing in high fire hazard zones.
